rows.notes: The cited document is a systematic review (narrative synthesis of 148 records on climate change impacts on coffee), not a primary study; Q1 is 'no'. It reports no own data on drip or sensor-based irrigation; irrigation appears only as a keyword in the PICO outcome list (Table 2) and in a passing reference to 'adequate water supply' citing another review [107]. It offers no evidence on drip irrigation as a drought-risk-management adaptation.

Systematic review, not a primary study; Q1 'no'. The document contains no results, own or synthesised, on rainwater harvesting or micro-irrigation for coffee; irrigation is mentioned only as a search keyword (Table 2/3) and in a cited remark about adequate water supply [107]. Nothing supports micro-irrigation as a climate-risk adaptation.

notes: Document is a complete MDPI Plants 2023 systematic review (Bilen et al.) with duplicated/garbled lines from the two-column PDF extraction but no apparent truncation. It is a review and makes no claims about drip or micro-irrigation; the citing review's attribution of irrigation adaptation recommendations to this source is not supported by its content.
